title: An interrupt right after landing_lock installs its SIGTERM handler, before the block that restores it opens, leaves the handler installed
goal: landing_lock restores the SIGTERM handler it replaced on an interrupt that lands right after the handler is installed

run:
import os, signal, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_close
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", t], check=True)
def mine(*_):
    pass
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, mine)
real = signal.signal
def interrupt_after_install(num, handler):
    old = real(num, handler)
    if handler is not mine and callable(handler):
        signal.signal = real
        raise KeyboardInterrupt
    return old
signal.signal = interrupt_after_install
try:
    with bl_close.landing_lock(t, "ST-aaaaaaaa"):
        pass
except BaseException as e:
    print("interrupted by", type(e).__name__)
finally:
    signal.signal = real
restored = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM) is mine
print("SIGTERM handler restored after an interrupt right after its install:", restored)
sys.exit(0 if restored else 1)
